sop-from-memo.output:
Water Heater Swap · You will need · Steps · Done looks like · Common mistakes.

YOU WILL NEED
- Water shutoff at main (building)
- Electrical breaker for heater
- Garden hose
- Floor drain access
- New flex lines (bring every time)
- Expansion tank (check for existing check valve on main line)
- Camera for photo documentation

STEPS

1. Shut the water at the main valve (do not rely on the small isolation valve alone). Listen for water flow to stop.

2. Kill the breaker for the heater. Verify power is off with a voltage tester.

3. Drain the tank into the floor drain using the garden hose from the van. Tank is empty when hose flow stops.

4. Disconnect the old flex lines and drain valve. Old unit is fully isolated from water and power.

5. Remove the old heater and position the new one in place. Unit is sitting level and stable.

6. Install new flex lines (replace every time, regardless of old line condition). All connections finger-tight, then wrench-snug.

7. Fill the new tank slowly through the cold-water inlet. Listen for water running at the outlet.

8. Bleed air at the closest hot-water faucet in the building. Water runs clear and steady from the tap.

9. Restore power at the breaker. Heater pilot or ignition lights.

10. Wait 20 minutes, then inspect every connection for drips or seepage. All connections are dry.

11. Take a photo of the installed unit for the job file. Photo is in the system.

COMMON MISTAKES

- Forgetting the expansion tank when a check valve exists on the main supply line. Always ask the owner or inspect the main before leaving. Check: look under the main shutoff for a small cylindrical tank with a valve on top.

- Turning power on before the tank is full and bled of air. This can damage the heating element. Check: hold your hand near the hot-water faucet after filling but before power — you should feel no heat yet.

- Checking for leaks too early (after 2 minutes instead of 20). Seals need time to settle. Check: return after 20 minutes minimum and inspect with a dry rag; any wet spots mean a connection needs tightening or resealing.
sop-from-memo.spoken: Water heater swap has eleven steps. Shut main water and breaker first, drain into the floor drain. Install new flex lines every time and bleed the air at the nearest hot tap before powering on. Wait twenty minutes then check for leaks; don't trust two minutes. Say read the rest to hear everything else.
